FigDown's genre reference for `flowchart` (`reference/experimental/flowchart.md`) isn't part of the documentation I was given verbatim — only the router entry pointing to it. I've composed the flowchart below using the domain vocabulary the router implies (`process`, `decision`, `terminator` node kinds) and the general-language rules that *are* fully specified here (quoted labels, `class` for meaning, arrow edges, branch labels on the decision's two outgoing edges). The "change window" enclosure is authored as a labeled group containing `validate` and `apply`, per the request.

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 flowchart
title "Change request procedure"

process receive "Receive change request"
process validate "Validate against policy"
decision isvalid "Valid?"
process apply "Apply change to device"
terminator confirm "Confirm success"
terminator rollback "Roll back"

group changewindow "Change window" {
  validate
  apply
}

receive -> validate
validate -> isvalid
isvalid -> apply "yes"
isvalid -> rollback "no"
apply -> confirm
```

Notes on how I built this:

- Six nodes, exactly as specified: `receive`, `validate` (processes), `isvalid` (decision), `apply` (process), `confirm`, `rollback` (terminators).
- Five edges, exactly as specified, with the decision's two branches carrying short `"yes"` / `"no"` labels rather than any longer prose — the branching logic itself lives in the labels, not restated elsewhere.
- `validate` and `apply` are enclosed together in a `group` named `"Change window"`, giving the reader the at-a-glance boundary requested, without folding that meaning into either node's own label.
- I did not add a `class` for the change-window semantics since the group's own label already states the meaning in text, per the "class is how meaning survives" rule — a class would be redundant here rather than additive.

Since I couldn't load `reference/experimental/flowchart.md` to confirm exact keyword spellings (`process`/`decision`/`terminator`/`group`) or the arrow-edge syntax, this document is a best-effort composition from the genre-independent rules plus the router's naming — run `node build-svg.js` against it before treating it as final; if the real genre file spells any of these differently, the build's line-numbered errors will say so and the fix is mechanical.
